question: A 3-day-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother because of irritability and feeding intolerance for 1 day. His temperature is 39.2°C (102.6°F). Physical examination shows a bulging anterior fontanelle. A photomicrograph of a Gram stain of the cerebrospinal fluid is shown. Further evaluation shows that the organism expresses the K1 capsular polysaccharide. Which of the following is the most likely causal pathogen?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Gram stain shows Gram-negative rods -> Organism expresses K1 capsular polysaccharide -> Likely causal pathogen is Escherichia coli -> 95%
CHAIN: Bulging anterior fontanelle -> Signs of meningitis -> Likely causal pathogen is Listeria monocytogenes -> 90%
enhanced_information: The most likely causal pathogen in this 3-day-old boy with irritability, feeding intolerance, high fever, and bulging anterior fontanelle expressing the K1 capsular polysaccharide is Escherichia coli, supported by the presence of Gram-negative rods and the specific capsular polysaccharide. Listeria monocytogenes is less likely despite its association with meningitis.
analysis: The core medical principle here is to identify the most likely causal pathogen causing meningitis in a 3-day-old infant with irritability, feeding intolerance, high fever, and a bulging anterior fontanelle. The enhanced information supports Escherichia coli as the most likely pathogen due to the presence of Gram-negative rods and the expression of the K1 capsular polysaccharide. Listeria monocytogenes is less likely in this scenario.
